chunks: You advanced towards me shouting “allegiance, allegiance” like she-camels having delivered newly born young ones leaping towards their young. I held back my hand but you pulled it towards you I drew back my hand but you dragged it. O my Allāh! these two have ignored my rights and did injustice to me. They both have broken allegiance to me, and roused people against me. Unfasten Thou what they have fastened, and do not make strong what they have woven. Show them the evil in what they aimed at and acted upon. Before fighting I asked them to be steadfast in allegiance and behaved with them with consideration but they belittled the blessing and refused (to adopt the course of) safety.

key_terms.قَطَعَانِي: ignored my rights / cut off my due

ai.seo_question: What is Imam Ali's description of Talha and Zubayr's allegiance in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) critiques the opportunistic nature of Talha and Zubayr’s allegiance, using the vivid metaphor of nursing camels to highlight their haste and lack of deliberation. This passage underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the legitimacy of his initial restraint and the subsequent breach of covenant (nukh) by the companions, framing the Battle of Jamal not merely as a political conflict but as a divine test of fidelity to the Prophet’s household.
